source.title: Communication regarding the update of the eDesk procedure: AML/CFT Market Entry Form (Funds and IFMs)

analysis.summary: The CSSF announced updates to the AML/CFT Market Entry Form workflow for funds and investment fund managers.
keyPoints: The communication clarifies which requests trigger a Market Entry Form submission.
Portfolio Manager and Investment Advisor sections were removed for authorised and registered IFMs.
businessTakeaways: The change affects the information prepared for market-entry requests rather than creating a new firm-wide AML programme.
Teams using saved forms or internal filing instructions may now be working from an outdated workflow.
suggestedActions: Compare current eDesk instructions and internal checklists with the updated procedure.
Review draft or reopened submissions to confirm that removed sections are no longer being populated.

source.title: The EBA launches its 2025 EU-wide transparency exercise

analysis.summary: The EBA launched its annual transparency exercise using supervisory reporting data from more than 100 major EU banks.
keyPoints: The exercise covers capital, financial assets, risk exposures, sovereign exposures and asset quality.
Results were scheduled for publication with the EBA Risk Assessment Report.
businessTakeaways: Participating banks should expect their supervisory reporting data to be presented in a comparable public dataset.
Data consistency and the explanation of visible movements may matter to finance and investor-relations teams.
suggestedActions: Confirm which submitted reporting periods and templates feed the exercise.
Prepare an internal reconciliation and narrative for material changes before results are published.

source.title: EBA issues revised list of ITS validation rules

analysis.summary: The EBA identified ITS validation rules that should be deactivated because of inaccuracies or technical problems.
keyPoints: Affected submissions should not be formally validated against deactivated rules.
A supporting package was published for consistent taxonomy and DPM updates.
businessTakeaways: Continuing to enforce a deactivated rule can create false submission failures and unnecessary remediation work.
The update is operationally relevant to both reporting logic and the supporting data model package.
suggestedActions: Identify the revised and deactivated rules in the EBA package.
Update local validation configuration and record the package version used for the next submission.

source.title: The EBA publishes draft amendments to the framework for reporting of MREL decisions by resolution authorities to the EBA

analysis.summary: Final draft amendments introduce more frequent MREL-decision reporting and update the reporting templates and methodology.
keyPoints: The proposed cycle becomes semi-annual instead of annual.
The amendments add detail on discretionary elements and reflect recent BRRD changes.
businessTakeaways: More frequent reporting can shorten the time available to reconcile MREL decisions and supporting data.
Template changes may affect established exchanges between resolution, treasury and reporting teams.
suggestedActions: Compare the draft templates and reporting frequency with the current internal process.
Identify data owners for the additional discretionary-element information.

source.title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/2180 of 12 September 2025 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2631 as regards external reviewers

analysis.summary: The delegated act specifies regulatory technical standards for registration, governance, staff expertise and outsourcing by external reviewers.
keyPoints: The act supplements the European Green Bond Regulation.
Requirements cover registration assessment and outsourcing conditions.
businessTakeaways: External reviewers may need to evidence governance, expertise and outsourcing arrangements during registration and ongoing supervision.
Firms relying on an external reviewer may want to understand whether the reviewer's operating model is affected.
suggestedActions: Map the standards against current registration and governance documentation.
Review outsourced activities, oversight arrangements and supporting records.

source.title: The ESAs note greater effort from financial market participants in their disclosure of principal adverse impacts

analysis.summary: The ESAs reported a general improvement in voluntary principal-adverse-impact disclosures under SFDR.
keyPoints: The review covered entity and product-level PAI statements.
The report includes recommendations for supervisors and the European Commission.
businessTakeaways: The report provides a supervisory benchmark for the clarity and completeness of current PAI disclosures.
Improvement across the market can raise expectations even where the publication itself does not create a new rule.
suggestedActions: Compare current entity- and product-level statements with the practices highlighted in the report.
Record disclosure gaps for the next SFDR reporting cycle and confirm ownership.
